title: Adaptive Stopping Rules for Probabilistic-Bit Classifiers with Autocorrelated Stochastic Magnetic Tunnel Junction Neurons
content: Probabilistic-bit (p-bit) classifiers built from stochastic magnetic tunnel junctions (sMTJs) are usually read at most once per two dwell times to keep reads nearly independent. Reading faster leaves each neuron’s firing probability unchanged but makes successive votes autocorrelated, which matters for adaptive inference that stops once the decision is declared settled. We simulate a p-bit multilayer perceptron whose hidden neurons follow two-state telegraph dynamics with the exact p-bit stationary law, and replay five stopping rules against the same recorded vote streams on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST. At half the correlation time, the stopping error on low-margin inputs of a Wald sequential probability ratio test and the Adaptive-Consistency Dirichlet rule, which treat votes as independent, rises three- to fourfold over ideal randomness, while whole-test accuracy moves at most 0.2 points. The cause is lost effective sample size. A Markov-chain likelihood calibrated once per operating point from unlabelled, reference-masked reads keeps error within the configured level down to one correlation time, reducing but not removing the excess over ideal randomness, at 1.3–1.4 times the throughput of throttled Adaptive-Consistency; an e-process does so without device measurement. Below one correlation time the correction’s compliance is partial, and re-estimating the correlation online per input is degenerate.
